title: Training Notes: Late Auto Insurance Renewals and Insurance Binder Acceptance on Wayfare Agreements
content:
These notes explain a rule of the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product on insurance binders: a Wayfare driver's history of late auto insurance renewals, shown by second expiry notices, shortens the binder acceptance days, the calendar days from the recording day for which a recorded binder is accepted as the auto insurance on file.

**Rule.** When the standing record holds three or more second expiry notices for the auto insurance dated fewer than 24 whole calendar months before the recording day, the binder acceptance days change by -10 days; when it holds exactly two, they change by -6 days; when it holds exactly one, they change by -3 days; when it holds none, they do not change.

| Second expiry notices for the auto insurance, dated fewer than 24 whole calendar months before the recording day | Change to the binder acceptance days |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | -10 |
| exactly 2 | -6 |
| exactly 1 | -3 |
| none | 0 |

### Questions answered

**Which notices count?** Only second expiry notices, and only those for the auto insurance. First notices, and notices for any other document, are not counted.

**How far back?** A notice counts when it is dated fewer than 24 whole calendar months before the recording day. A notice dated 24 whole calendar months or more before it does not count.

**Hypothetical example.** Recording day 2026-07-01. The standing record shows auto insurance second notices dated 2024-03-24, 2025-03-24 and 2026-03-24, and a first notice dated 2026-03-01. The notice of 2024-03-24 is more than 24 whole calendar months back; the first notice is not a second notice. Two notices count, so the binder acceptance days change by -6.
